name: Buspirone
route_note: Oral tablets two or three times daily; effect develops over 2–4 weeks.

discovery.by: Mead Johnson (Michael Eison, Yao Wu and colleagues)
discovery.note: Synthesised as a potential antipsychotic; it proved ineffective for psychosis but had anxiolytic activity.

tagline: Non-sedating, non-addictive anxiolytic acting on serotonin 5-HT1A receptors
summary: Buspirone is an azapirone anxiolytic used for generalised anxiety disorder. Unlike benzodiazepines it does not cause significant sedation, dependence or interaction with alcohol, but it takes weeks to work and is ineffective for acute anxiety or panic.
mechanism: Buspirone is a partial agonist at serotonin 5-HT1A receptors, acting as a near full agonist at presynaptic somatodendritic autoreceptors and a partial agonist at postsynaptic receptors. Gradual autoreceptor desensitisation increases serotonergic transmission.
It has weak dopamine D2 antagonist activity, and its metabolite 1-(2-pyrimidinyl)piperazine is an alpha-2 adrenergic antagonist. It does not act on GABA-A receptors.

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Buspirone is synthesised at Mead Johnson.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic buspirone launches in the US after patent litigation.

history.title: STAR*D
history.detail: In the STAR*D trial, buspirone is studied as an augmentation strategy for depression.

history.title: Gepirone
history.detail: The related azapirone gepirone (Exxua) is approved by the FDA for major depressive disorder.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic CYP3A4 to 1-PP and hydroxylated metabolites

facts: Grapefruit juice markedly increases buspirone levels by inhibiting intestinal CYP3A4.
